notes: SHIP v1.14.402 - OWNER RULING: THE VISIBILITY OBSERVER IS REDESIGN-HOUSE ONLY. This answers a flag raised against .401 rather than adding anything. THE FLAG. rackElevation_render3D is a SHARED renderer - it draws under ?legacy=1 as well as under body.rd - so the per-attachment IntersectionObserver that .401 installed at registration was changing runtime behaviour in the legacy house too. It changed no markup, no routing and no render output, and a paused loop resumes the moment its host is visible again, so nothing was broken by it. But rule 7 says ?legacy=1 is byte-identical-BEHAVIOUR, not merely byte-identical markup, and a loop that stops on a schedule it did not stop on before is a behaviour delta. It was disclosed at ship time rather than left silent, and the owner ruled: gate it. THE FIX. _observe now returns early unless document.body carries the rd class. Under ?legacy=1 no observer is created, att.paused stays false for the life of the attachment, and both renderers behave exactly as they did on .400 - each one's own document.hidden handler remains the only thing that can stop its loop, which is the .400 behaviour verbatim. The check is register-time, and that is sound because body.rd is added exactly ONCE, at boot, by redesign_initToggle at :18895, and is never removed or toggled at runtime - verified, it is the only add/remove/toggle site in the file. The class was chosen over redesign_isOn() deliberately: redesign_isOn WRITES phantom_legacy to localStorage as a side effect of parsing the URL, and a hot lifecycle path is the wrong place for a storage write. The class is also the more precise question - it asks whether the redesign frame is actually mounted rather than whether it was requested. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, AND WHY. The single-live-context guard - RackEngine.releaseOthers, invariant I1 - stays global and applies in BOTH houses. Two live WebGL contexts on iOS is the exact crash class this entire milestone exists to close, and the legacy house is entitled to that fix; gating it would mean shipping a known defect to legacy on purpose. Only the OBSERVER is house-scoped. The invariant is not. That split is written into the code at the gate so nobody widens it later by accident. HONESTY NOTE: the early return is not a No-Silent-Failures violation. It is the ruled behaviour on an internal lifecycle path with no user-facing surface, not an error being swallowed, and RackEngine.report() still lists the attachment in either house so the census stays truthful about what is live. Three .401 comments that described the observer as applying to every host were corrected in the same pass rather than left to drift. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, node --check sw.js, version.json valid JSON, CSS braces 4557/4557 delta 0, line endings unchanged all-LF, PRECACHE untouched, three-stamp lockstep, diff confined to RackEngine._observe plus three comments. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) bare URL, open Build, leave for Tools, return - PhantomGL.diag() must still show the attachment reporting paused true while away and false on return, exactly as .401 did. (2) Load ?legacy=1, reach a rack surface, and confirm the rack renders and keeps rendering as it did before .401; RackEngine.report() should list the attachment with paused false throughout. (3) Clear phantom_legacy between the two - a ?legacy=1 visit pins it for the whole origin and the next tab boots legacy by design.
